intro_html: Florentine on a menu means there is spinach in it, a naming convention we inherited from French kitchens honoring Catherine de Medici. What it means for your kitchen is that frozen chopped spinach, which costs almost nothing, is about to carry a creamy turkey bake. Each serving lands at 572 calories with 35 grams of protein for about $3.79 (at everyday cost). There is a whisper of curry powder in the sauce that sounds strange and tastes exactly right.
cost_closing_html: About $3.79 a serving (at everyday cost). Frozen spinach and rice are two of the cheapest things you can put on a plate, and the mushroom cream sauce makes them taste expensive.
shop_smart: Frozen chopped spinach in 10 oz boxes costs a fraction of fresh spinach for the same cooked volume. Fresh would need several pounds to equal what five boxes deliver here.
Squeeze the thawed spinach dry in a clean towel before it goes in. Skipping this is how a cream sauce turns into a puddle, and wasted sauce is wasted money.
White mushrooms in 8 oz packs beat pre-sliced on price every time. Slicing three packs takes about five minutes.
Rice from the big bag is the cheapest base you can build a casserole on, and it never spoils on the shelf.
make_it: Weigh your empty mixing pot and write the number down for portioning later.
Cook the rice and spread it across the bottom of a greased 9x13 pan as the base layer.
Thaw the frozen chopped spinach and squeeze it dry in a clean kitchen towel, wringing hard. You want a compact ball, not a wet clump.
Melt the butter in a large pot over medium heat, add the diced onion and sliced mushrooms, and cook 8 to 10 minutes until the mushroom liquid cooks away.
Whisk in the flour and cook two minutes, then add the chicken broth and the milk gradually, whisking, and cook until the sauce thickens.
Season with salt, black pepper, and the curry powder. It is a small amount and it is what separates this from every other cream sauce.
Off the heat, melt in most of the shredded cheese, then fold in the squeezed spinach and the diced turkey breast.
Pour the sauce over the rice, top with the remaining cheese, and bake at 375F for 30 minutes until bubbling and browned, then rest 10 minutes before portioning.
portion_html: Set the pan on the scale, subtract the empty pan weight, and divide by 14. Cut through the rice base and the creamed spinach layer together so every container gets both. Each serving comes to 572 calories and 35 grams of protein.

head.description: Turkey Florentine rice bake meal prep: creamed spinach and mushroom sauce with turkey over a rice base. 572 calories, 35g protein, about $3.79 a serving (at everyday cost).
head.keywords: turkey florentine, creamed spinach casserole, spinach rice bake, leftover turkey recipes, budget meal prep, high protein casserole
steps: Cook the rice and spread it into a greased 9x13 pan.
Thaw and wring the frozen spinach completely dry.
Cook the onion and mushrooms in butter until dry, whisk in the flour, then add the broth and milk and cook until thick.
Season with salt, pepper, and curry powder, melt in most of the cheese off the heat, and fold in the spinach and turkey.
Pour over the rice, top with the rest of the cheese, bake at 375F for 30 minutes, rest 10 minutes, and portion into 14 containers.
